summary: A cut that took nothing out (same recording, same speed, the second side starting on the frame the first stopped on) can be joined back into one piece from its right-click or from Clip ▸ Join Through Edit, without Undo throwing away everything done since.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/join-through-edit-walk.json.

try.do: Open the sample recording and put the playhead at 4 s.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press ⌘K (or B for the Blade and click at 4 s) to cut the clip.
Right-click the cut and choose Join Through Edit.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press ⌘Z once: the cut comes back.
Put Dip to black on the cut, then Join Through Edit again.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Cut at 4 s and 6 s, delete the piece between, and right-click the cut left behind.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick a cut and open the Clip menu: Join Through Edit sits under Roll Edit to Playhead.

evaluate: Is Join Through Edit where you would reach for it, at the foot of the cut's right-click under Roll Edit to Playhead?
When a transition is on the cut, is the short 'Joined · Dip to black taken off' note enough to tell you what went?
On a jump cut the row is there but dimmed: does that read as 'not here', or would you rather it were hidden?
After the join you are left holding the joined piece; is that what you expected?
rough: No mock draws this row; it follows Premiere's Join Through Edit name and has no key, as Premiere gives it none (UX-PATTERNS §7).
Delete on a picked through edit does not join it, as it does in Premiere; the task asked not to change Delete without a card, so it is left as it was.
B in Next picks the Blade tool, as Premiere's razor does, so the task's 'press B at 4 s' is B and a click at 4 s, or ⌘K at the playhead.
Between two separate clips of one recording the join keeps the earlier clip's name, effects and keys; the later clip's keys are dropped, as Premiere drops the second clip's attributes.
